Manville plays a British professor visiting Poland in 1981, who is suddenly swept up in extraordinary and dangerous events at the onset of the country’s Martial Law era. The film is a thrilling and immersive cat-and-mouse game, inspired by the short story by Booker Prize and Nobel Prize winning author Olga Tokarczuk.

One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

Formally and structurally audacious, in its rich color palette and its free movement between slice-of-life realism to transcendental mysticism, and throughout deeply humane.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem

Haunted by the unceasing hum of tinnitus in her left ear and sudden death of her twin sister, Wahida (El Fadul) goes to the remote Ras Al-Khaimah mountains to find solace. Instead, she comes across an eerie green door in her sister’s locked bedroom that seems to blur the line between reality and fantasy, and the living and the dead. In Nayla Al Khaja’s dark fairy tale, an immersive exploration of grief, the audience is plunged into Wahida’s shattered mind, and seemingly ordinary domestic spaces are transformed into an emotional landscape of fear and trauma. Even scarier than the film’s psychological horror-trip is the fact that it has been so hard to see outside of the region in which it was made. Despite al Khaja’s breakthrough talent as the first female Emirati filmmaker, the delighted reviews out of Baab’s premiere at the Cairo International Film Festival, a theatrical run throughout the MENA world, and a collaboration with two-time Oscar award-winning Indian film composer A.R. screenings.title: The Scout
screenings.description: Director González-Nasser spent six years working as a location scout. In this luminous directorial debut, she brings us into a day in the life of a young scout tasked with finding the perfect interiors for a television pilot. Sofía (Mimi Davila) moves in and out of other people’s intimate spaces and quotidian lives, tweaking her personality just enough to connect while struggling to find balance between her professional and personal worlds. With a mounting stack of parking tickets and the impertinent commentaries of her crew, she faces a series of small-yet-paralyzing obstacles that render her day increasingly exhausting. Through a constellation of quiet but poignant vignettes, the film offers an original view into the invisible labor of TV production, unfolding as an alternative symphony of a New York grappling with gentrification and a growing erosion of empathy. screenings.title: First We Bombed New Mexico - the Aftermath
screenings.description: The inspiring story of a relentless Latina cancer survivor who takes on 80 years of injustice by the U.S. government. Tina Cordova catalyzes a movement to secure acknowledgement and compensation for the ignored Native American and Hispanic cancer victims of the Trinity Bomb’s radioactive fallout. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH exposes the racism and nuclear colonization that enabled New Mexico to become America’s nuclear bomb–making state. The film screens during a moment of grave global insecurity. This film personalizes the unthinkable human cost of another nuclear incident. One day, fed up with her stuffy, small-minded neighbors, she commissions herself a husband to be made from wicker. In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

screenings.title: Nous (We)
screenings.description: A Malian mechanic; the filmmaker’s sister, a healthcare worker; the acclaimed author Pierre Bergounioux; banlieue teenagers playing Uno… What ties the disparate subjects of Diop’s film together is, in one sense, geographical happenstance—they all live in proximity to the RER B line that runs northeast to southwest—but in following the contours of the commuter train, she gives a panoramic view of another Paris, far from postcard views of the 16 arrondissements.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: Your Mother Your Mother Your Mother
screenings.description: From writer-director Bassam Tariq, YOUR MOTHER YOUR MOTHER YOUR MOTHER stars Mahershala Ali as Latif, a devoutly religious hitman who struggles to balance work, faith and fatherhood. When his wife dies, he embarks on a desperate journey across Houston to protect his children, confronting the forces closing in around him - and the beliefs threatening to unravel within.

screenings.title: Possible Love
screenings.description: A story of two married couples — a laid-off worker and his spouse and a documentary filmmaker and her spouse — crossing paths to film a documentary and facing their different lives and hidden desires.

screenings.title: The Social Reckoning
screenings.description: A companion piece to the hit film The Social Network, Sorkin’s original screenplay tells the true story of how Frances Haugen (Mikey Madison), a young Facebook engineer, enlists the help of Jeff Horwitz (Jeremy Allen White), a Wall Street Journal reporter, to go on a dangerous journey that ends up blowing the whistle on the social network’s most guarded secrets.

screenings.title: Hellraiser
screenings.description: “We have such sights to show you…” In horror polymath Clive Barker’s adaptation of his novella The Hellbound Heart, horny hedonist Uncle Frank plays with a mysterious puzzle box, summons the Cenobites (led by Doug Bradley in an iconic performance) and endangers his unsuspecting niece (Ashley Laurence). A work of remarkable specificity and imagination, this inimitable, hot and bothered horror landmark is presented in a new 4K restoration.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: Sweet Rush
screenings.description: Tatarak Poland, 2009 Directed by Andrzej Wajda Starring Krystyna Janda, Paweł Szajda Approx. 85 mins. An aging married woman (Krystyna Janda), who lost two sons during the war, becomes fascinated with a strapping young man she encounters one day. In this self-reflexive meditation on death, and the passion of youth, Janda breaks the film’s fourth wall with a powerful monologue on the death of her real-life husband, Edward Kłosiński (who happened to be the cinematographer of Wajda’s MAN OF MARBLE and MAN OF IRON). Experimental in structure, this moving film is itself beautifully lensed by Paweł Edelman, frequent Wajda collaborator who also shot Polański’s THE PIANIST and THE GHOST WRITER. Presented with support from The Ashes and Diamonds Fund for Eastern European Film

screenings.title: Magic
screenings.description: Dir. Richard Attenborough. 1978, 107 mins. U.S. 35mm. With Anthony Hopkins, Ann-Margret, Burgess Meredith, Ed Lauter. In this sinister cult classic, a brilliantly unbalanced Anthony Hopkins plays Charles “Corky” Withers, a failed magician turned ventriloquist who begins to show symptoms of psychosis—and allows his dummy, the foul-mouthed “Fats,” to take over his life. Is he shuttling head-first into a mental crackup? Or does the mean-spirited Fats truly have a mind of his own? Genuinely unsettling, this shadowy, emotionally gripping thriller was infamous for its 1970s TV spots, which scarred a generation of unsuspecting kids, but the film is diabolically effective in every way, and features a stellar cast, including a touching Ann-Margret as his love interest. Tickets: $17.50 / $12 senior and students / $10 youth / free for MoMI members. There is a $1.50 transaction fee per ticket for all online purchases. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Fist Church
screenings.description: Every other Sunday we’ll be mining the depths of VHS, VCD, DVD, and the darkest corners of the internet to bring you the wildest post-brunch experience you’re likely to have. So, get faded on Bloody Mary’s (leave the PCP at home) and come kick your feet up while we play fast and loose with the rules and witness people fight hopping vampires, ninjas, swordsmen and more. The movies won’t be announced, but trust us – on this one we wouldn’t steer you wrong.

screenings.title: La Bola Negra in 35mm
screenings.description: From Cannes-winning directors Javier Calvo and Javier Ambrossi — popularly known as Los Javis —LA BOLA NEGRA follows three generations of men across pivotal moments in Spanish history, bound by pain, desire, and love. Carlos (Milo Quifes) longs to belong in a fractured Spain. Sebastián (Guitarricadelafuente) finds connection across enemy lines. And Alberto (Carlos González) uncovers a long-buried family secret — one that finally gives voice to truths the past tried to erase.

screenings.title: Wildwood in 35mm
screenings.description: Wildwood is a handcrafted epic fantasy that transports audiences into a secret, dangerously alive world. A girl’s desperate quest to save her baby brother unfolds into a spectacular, high-stakes adventure through a forbidden forest full of enchanted creatures, endearing allies, and formidable adversaries—where an entire hidden realm hangs in the balance. In an era of automation, LAIKA delivers its most ambitious and globally accessible film yet—a bold fusion of human-crafted artistry and cinematic storytelling from the makers of Coraline.

screenings.description: From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

screenings.title: Girl, Interrupted
screenings.description: Based on a 1993 memoir of the same name by Susanna Kaysen, Mangold’s powerhouse picture sets its scene at a New England psychiatric hospital c. 1967 where Winona Ryder (in the Kaysen role; also a producer on the film) lands after suffering a nervous breakdown. Among the committed at Claymoore are a hall-of-fame lineup of ’90s female acting talent, including self-harmer Brittany Murphy, schizophrenic burn victim Elisabeth Moss and, in a star-making turn, Angelina Jolie as sociopath agitator Lisa Rowe. Ryder’s is not the flashiest role here, but she holds the film together with her quiet, alert intensity, offering a springboard for her co-stars to dive off into the deep end.

The Devils
screenings.description: Assembled from the original camera negative, this new 4K restoration presents Ken Russell’s definitive vision of The Devils by referencing the edit he privately constructed in 2004. The film’s sound has been remastered from original English Composite 35mm Mag Film, transferred at 96kHz, plus other original film elements in selected spots as needed. The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

screenings.title: Making Marie Antoinette
screenings.description: In 2005, Eleanor Coppola filmed her daughter Sofia directing Marie Antoinette at the Palace of Versailles, the first production ever granted access to the palace. For two decades, eighty hours of footage went unseen. Now, twenty years after the film’s release and in fulfillment of her mother’s wish, that footage becomes a film of its own. Making Marie Antoinette follows the making of this landmark production, Milena Canonero’s costume work, and what it took to direct at 34, watched the whole time by her own mother.

screenings.title: My Undesirable Friends: Part Ii – Exile: Chapters 4-5
screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “Gripping... Expect to find yourself riveted... Grand in scale but entirely intimate in scope, what she’s achieved here is a landmark work that will go down as one of the boldest documentary achievements of the 21st century.” – Ryan Lattanzio, IndieWire “A riveting and vital portrait of media courage under fire. It’s as must-see as they get.” – Nick Schager, Daily Beast CRITIC’S PICK. “Essential. Riveting.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Monumental... It’s great cinema.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine/Vulture “The follow-up to 2024’s LAST AIR IN MOSCOW proves every bit as compelling, if more intimate... EXILE deepens the viewer’s connection to Loktev’s journalists while introducing engaging new subjects... Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Speaking truth to power with the online tools at their disposal, this murderer’s row consists of lively, awkward, driven, beautiful, lovestruck, and above-all complicated people, all caught in impossible personal and professional deadlocks and weighed down by immigrant uncertainty.” – Siddhant Adlakha, Variety “STAGGERING. GRIPPING. [A] massive monument to journalism, competing in length and ambition with legendary feats of nonfiction like SHOAH and the UP series... a celebration of truth in an endless fight against deception.” – Jacob Oller, AV Club “An essential chronicle of reporters under fire... Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. The film’s final chapter has the charge of an espionage thriller.” – Marshall Shaffer, Slant “BRILLIANT. Keeping us on the edge of our seats for 6 hours. A moving tribute to the necessity of resistance.” – Boris Bastide, Le Monde

screenings.title: First We Bombed New Mexico - the Aftermath
screenings.description: The inspiring story of a relentless Latina cancer survivor who takes on 80 years of injustice by the U.S. government. Tina Cordova catalyzes a movement to secure acknowledgement and compensation for the ignored Native American and Hispanic cancer victims of the Trinity Bomb’s radioactive fallout. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH exposes the racism and nuclear colonization that enabled New Mexico to become America’s nuclear bomb–making state. The film screens during a moment of grave global insecurity. This film personalizes the unthinkable human cost of another nuclear incident. An earlier version of the film won 16 festival awards, including Best Director and Best Documentary at the Paris Cine Film Festival, Best Documentary Feature and Best Directing at the Worldwide Women’s Film Festival, and the Jury Prize for Best Historical Documentary at the San Antonio Film Festival. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH reveals an unknown story that has captured audiences. The film was a part of the momentum that led to Congress awarding compensation to New Mexico Downwinder families in 2025. The inspirational re-release witnesses a people who were once considered powerless and voiceless finally gaining recognition after years of fighting for justice.

screenings.title: Miss Representation: Rise Up
screenings.description: Over a decade after MISS REPRESENTATION exposed the media’s contribution to the underrepresentation of women in leadership, this follow-up dives deep into the cultural backlash against women’s agency and power. With the proliferation of AI and deepfakes, a new era of tech-facilitated violence is exacerbating sexism and misogyny in an attempt to control and silence women and girls. With inspiring young women at its core, MISS REPRESENTATION: RISE UP interweaves their personal journeys with powerful voices in media, culture, leadership, and academia to reimagine a future that finally uplifts women and girls.

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: “One of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I've ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker CRITIC’S PICK. “A house party for the ages... A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... A truly monumental work of art.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “The stuff of legend... Feels like a miracle.” – Robert Daniels, RogerEbert.com “An atmospheric, electrifying documentary, and a moving testament to the importance of remembering.” – Shirley Li, The Atlantic “An intergenerational feat... A documentary brimming with the wise, the thought-provoking and the deeply entertaining... [A] glimmering gift... with something that resembles a calling forth of the ancestors... A vivid and layered time capsule... Turns viewers into time travelers but also invited guests, rightly grateful to be in the room. For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. A triumph of DIY filmmaking and an act of cinematic resistance.” – Jourdain Searles, The Hollywood Reporter “A masterpiece.” – David Fear, Rolling Stone “Not only the biggest surprise of this year’s Sundance, but a revelation.” – Chris O’Falt, IndieWire

Please note that broadcasts in some territories are scheduled later to accommodate local time zones.

screenings.title: La Raulito
screenings.description: “I feel like I’m in a perpetual quest to discover new (old) films depicting transmasc, butch, and gender nonconforming characters and stories. I first came across La Raulito in 2022, but it’s taken all these years to finally track it down and be able to show it. Like all of the films in this series, La Raulito has a wonderful quality of melodramatic earnestness. As someone who has always embraced sincerity in my own work as a filmmaker, I think this is one of the most beautiful and brave examples you’ll ever see of telling the story of a hero (a real-life national hero in Argentina) who you absolutely cannot resist falling in love with.” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist

screenings.description: The most powerful man in the world races to prove he is humanity’s savior before the disaster he unleashed destroys everything.

screenings.title: On the Relentless Destruction of Beauty: Short Housing Films + Q&A
screenings.description: On The Relentless Destruction of Beauty features artist studios, communized parks, and residential buildings as spaces produced through—and for—collective creativity, labor, and cohabitation. Spanning the 1960s to the present, the program traces the ways everyday acts of living and making come into conflict with capital’s logic of private property, which seeks to empty such spaces of life in the pursuit of profit. Across these four films, however, the home emerges not as a commodity to be exchanged—nor as an asset to be valued through speculation and dispossession—but as a site of ongoing creative struggle.

screenings.title: Demonic Umbrella Aka Midnight Conjure
screenings.description: The two films, THE CHINESE GHOSTBUSTER and EXORCIST MASTER (the latter screened as part of our 2023 Fist Fright Marathon) would mark the last time Lam would appear on the big screen as his Taoist priest character, and curiously, both films provide a more in-depth look at Taoist ritual and practice than most of his previous appearances. CHINESE GHOSTBUSTER is largely a riff on the Taoist folk legend of Zhong Kui, a mythological demon slayer known as the “King of Ghosts”, while EXORCIST MASTER operates on a playful contrast between the religious traditions of its two leads, a Taoist priest played by Lam, and a Christian priest played by Wu. Together the films offer a fittingly spiritual coda to the career of a performer whose likeness inadvertently became synonymous with the Taoism itself.

screenings.description: Followed by a conversation with filmmakers and special guests Dirs. Sarita Khurana and Yoav Attias. 2026, 90 mins. U.S. DCP. Seat at the Table chronicles the rise of South Asian Americans in U.S. politics, tracing a remarkable journey from political disenfranchisement to an increasingly powerful presence in American civic life. Filmed during the 2024 election cycle, Khurana and Attias follow congressional and state-level candidates alongside grassroots organizers, voters, and communities as a record number of South Asian Americans seek elected office. With intimate vérité access, the film captures a community awakening to its political power at a pivotal moment in American democracy. Moving beyond individual campaigns, Seat at the Table explores representation, belonging, and the ways immigrant communities are reshaping who participates in, and ultimately holds power within, American political life. The screening will be followed by a conversation with the filmmakers and special guests about the making of the documentary, South Asian political representation, and the communities helping to redefine who has a seat at the table in American civic life. Free with RSVP.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: First We Bombed New Mexico - the Aftermath
screenings.description: The inspiring story of a relentless Latina cancer survivor who takes on 80 years of injustice by the U.S. government. Tina Cordova catalyzes a movement to secure acknowledgement and compensation for the ignored Native American and Hispanic cancer victims of the Trinity Bomb’s radioactive fallout. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH exposes the racism and nuclear colonization that enabled New Mexico to become America’s nuclear bomb–making state. The film screens during a moment of grave global insecurity. This film personalizes the unthinkable human cost of another nuclear incident. An earlier version of the film won 16 festival awards, including Best Director and Best Documentary at the Paris Cine Film Festival, Best Documentary Feature and Best Directing at the Worldwide Women’s Film Festival, and the Jury Prize for Best Historical Documentary at the San Antonio Film Festival. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH reveals an unknown story that has captured audiences. The film was a part of the momentum that led to Congress awarding compensation to New Mexico Downwinder families in 2025. The inspirational re-release witnesses a people who were once considered powerless and voiceless finally gaining recognition after years of fighting for justice.

screenings.description: “When Caden Mark Gardner and I co-curated Vera as part of the original Masc series in 2022, Caden did some amazing research on the film. Together we determined that it is one of the earliest (and also one of the best) portrayals in world cinema of a transmasculine character. And the film’s protagonist, Bauer (the film’s title is his dead name), shines through as an incredible transmasc hero. As he confidently proclaims to the powers that be, ‘I’m not what everyone thinks I am. You hear me? I’m different. I’m something else. Something else.’” —Series curator Jenni Olson, queer film historian and archivist

Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Speaking truth to power with the online tools at their disposal, this murderer’s row consists of lively, awkward, driven, beautiful, lovestruck, and above-all complicated people, all caught in impossible personal and professional deadlocks and weighed down by immigrant uncertainty.” – Siddhant Adlakha, Variety “STAGGERING. GRIPPING. Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. screenings.title: One in a Million
screenings.description: Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home?

Seder cohosted an earlier edition of his show The Majority Report in 2004 alongside actress/comedian Janeane Garofalo. The discussion will reach back to the era of the Patriot Act, the Iraq War, what it was like to be skeptical of the direction of America under the George W. Bush admin… and the repercussions of it today.

screenings.title: Making Marie Antoinette
screenings.description: In 2005, Eleanor Coppola filmed her daughter Sofia directing Marie Antoinette at the Palace of Versailles, the first production ever granted access to the palace. For two decades, eighty hours of footage went unseen. Now, twenty years after the film’s release and in fulfillment of her mother’s wish, that footage becomes a film of its own. Making Marie Antoinette follows the making of this landmark production, Milena Canonero’s costume work, and what it took to direct at 34, watched the whole time by her own mother.

screenings.title: Azul
screenings.description: AZUL is a documentary about the poetic soul of Nicaragua. Twenty-four poems interweave with interviews to create a narrative of Nicaragua’s poetry and the historical contexts and individuals who formed it. With poems from the creator of Modernismo, Rubén Darío, to Ernesto Cardenal, Carlos Rigby, and Gioconda Belli, to people reciting spontaneously in the street and soldiers workshopping poems on the frontlines, AZUL reveals a nation alive with the creative spirit and a profound belief in poetry as a crucible for change and expression. Originally filmed during the height of the Contra War, the film has been restored digitally.Preceded by:Richard Levine AFTER BASHŌ 2026, 8 min, DCPTwenty haikus by Bob Holman – written while he was following “A Narrow Path Into the Interior,” the walk that Japan’s National Poet, Matsuo Bashō, took in 1689 – are the starting point of this animated collaboration by filmmaker Richard Levine, musician Phillip Johnston, and poet Bob Holman. The poems originally appeared in The New Yorker magazine.Followed by a Q&A with co-producer and editor Joanna Kiernan!CLICK HERE TO BUY TICKETS NOW!

It’s a crime melodrama, with most of the attendant clichés accounted for and transcended, especially of the last job before retirement from the underworld. It’s a star vehicle, with Pacino riding high at the crest of a resurgence that began with Harold Becker’s superb 1989 thriller SEA OF LOVE and would continue through the 1990s and into the early aughts. It’s also a character study, filled to the brim with actors doing astonishing work—among them Sean Penn, Viggo Mortensen, John Leguizamo, and Luis Guzmán—with an unusual anecdotal structure. Vignettes interlock in surprising fashion, filling in the contours of Puerto Rican gangster Carlito’s life as he emerges from prison and is hit up by everyone for favors.” – Roger Ebert Presented with support from The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.description: Chris Shields is a film critic and filmmaker based in Los Angeles. As a writer he frequently contributes to Sight and Sound, Reverse Shot, Film Comment, Screen Slate, Cineaste, Vinegar Syndrome, Cinematographe, LARB, and a host of other film publications. As a filmmaker he has a large body of experimental video work that has screened around the world including at Chicago Underground Film Festival and Winnipeg Underground Film Festival. His experimental film, Channels, is featured on the streaming platform Paracme. He is the co-writer and co-star of Lindsay Denniberg’s cult favorite Video Diary of a Lost Girl (available from AGFA and Vinegar Syndrome) and her forthcoming feature Killer Makeover. He is also a moderator for the American Cinematheque, conducting Q and As with filmmakers such as Jon Jost and Tsai Ming-liang. As a musician he performed for years as Mr. Transylvania, a punk/noise performance project, and in the bands United Waters and Alien Trilogy. He has also had every minimum wage job imaginable, including pizza delivery. Morbid Weekend is his feature directorial debut.

screenings.description: Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home?

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

screenings.title: The Devils

The Picture and Sound restoration was performed by Warner Bros. Post Production Creative Services, Water Tower Color, and Warner Bros. Sound.

screenings.title: The Great Experiment

THE GREAT EXPERIMENT is an epic poem in documentary form – a mirror held to an American nation at war with its own reflection, asking not who is right, but whether the experiment itself can survive.

screenings.title: Possible Love

screenings.title: Man of Marble
screenings.description: Człowiek z marmuru Poland, 1977 Directed by Andrzej Wajda Starring Krystyna Janda, Jerzy Radziwiłowicz, Tadeusz Łomnicki, Approx. 161 mins. An aggressive documentary filmmaker fights present-day 1970s government censorship as she seeks the truth about bricklayer Matuesz Birkut, a state-manufactured proletariat hero during the Soviet-controlled 1950s. Fourteen years in the making, MAN OF MARBLE is a film-within-a-film that blends documentary, pseudo-documentary, and fictional techniques that inevitably draw comparison to CITIZEN KANE. Like Orson Welles’ masterpiece, MAN OF MARBLE is a reflection on national history and mythology and also on the very nature of filmmaking. It also turned out to prophesize the worker strikes of 1980 and the rise of the Solidarity movement. Presented with support from The Ashes and Diamonds Fund for Eastern European Film

screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “Gripping... Expect to find yourself riveted... Grand in scale but entirely intimate in scope, what she’s achieved here is a landmark work that will go down as one of the boldest documentary achievements of the 21st century.” – Ryan Lattanzio, IndieWire “A riveting and vital portrait of media courage under fire. It’s as must-see as they get.” – Nick Schager, Daily Beast CRITIC’S PICK. “Essential. Riveting.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Monumental... It’s great cinema.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine/Vulture “The follow-up to 2024’s LAST AIR IN MOSCOW proves every bit as compelling, if more intimate... Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. The film’s final chapter has the charge of an espionage thriller.” – Marshall Shaffer, Slant “BRILLIANT. Keeping us on the edge of our seats for 6 hours. A moving tribute to the necessity of resistance.” – Boris Bastide, Le Monde

screenings.title: The Scout
screenings.description: Director González-Nasser spent six years working as a location scout. In this luminous directorial debut, she brings us into a day in the life of a young scout tasked with finding the perfect interiors for a television pilot. Sofía (Mimi Davila) moves in and out of other people’s intimate spaces and quotidian lives, tweaking her personality just enough to connect while struggling to find balance between her professional and personal worlds. With a mounting stack of parking tickets and the impertinent commentaries of her crew, she faces a series of small-yet-paralyzing obstacles that render her day increasingly exhausting. Through a constellation of quiet but poignant vignettes, the film offers an original view into the invisible labor of TV production, unfolding as an alternative symphony of a New York grappling with gentrification and a growing erosion of empathy. Presented with support from The Endowed Fund for Emerging Filmmakers 2025 89 MIN. USA GREENWICH ENTERTAINMENT Open Caption (OC) Screenings: Saturday, October 17, 2:10 show Monday, October 19, 2:10 show

screenings.title: First We Bombed New Mexico - the Aftermath
screenings.description: The inspiring story of a relentless Latina cancer survivor who takes on 80 years of injustice by the U.S. government. Tina Cordova catalyzes a movement to secure acknowledgement and compensation for the ignored Native American and Hispanic cancer victims of the Trinity Bomb’s radioactive fallout. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH exposes the racism and nuclear colonization that enabled New Mexico to become America’s nuclear bomb–making state. The film screens during a moment of grave global insecurity. This film personalizes the unthinkable human cost of another nuclear incident. An earlier version of the film won 16 festival awards, including Best Director and Best Documentary at the Paris Cine Film Festival, Best Documentary Feature and Best Directing at the Worldwide Women’s Film Festival, and the Jury Prize for Best Historical Documentary at the San Antonio Film Festival. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH reveals an unknown story that has captured audiences. The film was a part of the momentum that led to Congress awarding compensation to New Mexico Downwinder families in 2025. The inspirational re-release witnesses a people who were once considered powerless and voiceless finally gaining recognition after years of fighting for justice.

screenings.title: Naza
screenings.description: We made this film out of a sense of obligation to use our position as Israeli filmmakers and journalists to examine the systems behind the mass killing of Palestinian civilians for which our country is responsible. While filming members of Israel’s military on rooftops at night in Tel Aviv over the past three years, we found ourselves asking the very questions that were asked by our grandparents’ generation and throughout the 20th century: how does one group of people allow the total dehumanization of another? What do the inner workings of such a system look like? Many of the revelations in the film were published almost immediately as we learned of them, in the months following the October 7th attacks, by The Guardian (one of NAZA’s producers), in collaboration with reporting partners +972 Magazine and Local Call. The film lets us explore something deeper than we could in our investigative journalism alone: not only the words being said but also those that are not said, the silence. It is up to all of us to break that silence.

Their teenage children form a fast bond with a neighboring family as unease begins to simmer around their rigid beliefs. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

screenings.title: Little Women
screenings.description: Winona Ryder would receive an Academy Award nomination for Best Actress for her role as the headstrong, literary minded Jo March in Armstrong’s perfectly enchanting adaptation of Louisa May Alcott’s 1868 novel of the same name, about the travails of the March sisters of Concord, Massachusetts, and their various suitors. Made with sweet-spirited good humor and exacting attention to period detail, with Trini Alvarado, Samantha Mathis, Kirsten Dunst, and Claire Danes rounding out the March clan, and Eric Stoltz, Gabriel Byrne, and Christian Bale among the men drawn to the glow exuded by the March homestead. “Solid, warming, bountiful, brimful of high spirits, a glowing treat that belongs at the top of any holiday movie shopping list.” —Boston Globe

screenings.title: Arsenal
screenings.description: The film that made Dovzhenko’s international reputation, Arsenal depicts—in thrillingly innovative, lyric cinematic language—a 1918 episode in the Russian Civil War, a worker’s uprising at Kyiv’s Arsenal Factory, and its brutal military suppression, in the midst of fighting between Bolshevik forces and the Central Rada of the Ukrainian People’s Republic, in whose ranks Dovzhenko may have served for a time. One of a quartet of films commissioned by Soviet authorities to celebrate the 10th anniversary of the October Revolution and, of the four, the most ambivalent, showing an understanding, in turns, of both the universalist, workers-of-the-world-unite Bolshevik cause and a Ukrainian nationalism rooted in soul and soil.

screenings.title: Sweet Rush
screenings.description: Tatarak Poland, 2009 Directed by Andrzej Wajda Starring Krystyna Janda, Paweł Szajda Approx. 85 mins. An aging married woman (Krystyna Janda), who lost two sons during the war, becomes fascinated with a strapping young man she encounters one day. In this self-reflexive meditation on death, and the passion of youth, Janda breaks the film’s fourth wall with a powerful monologue on the death of her real-life husband, Edward Kłosiński (who happened to be the cinematographer of Wajda’s MAN OF MARBLE and MAN OF IRON). Experimental in structure, this moving film is itself beautifully lensed by Paweł Edelman, frequent Wajda collaborator who also shot Polański’s THE PIANIST and THE GHOST WRITER. Presented with support from The Ashes and Diamonds Fund for Eastern European Film

screenings.description: Paranoid Brigadier General Jack D. Ripper of Burpelson Air Force Base, believing that fluoridation of the American water supply is a Soviet plot to poison the U.S. populace, is able to deploy through a back door mechanism a nuclear attack on the Soviet Union without the knowledge of his superiors, including the Chair of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, General Buck Turgidson, and President Merkin Muffley. Only Ripper knows the code to recall the B-52 bombers and he has shut down communication in and out of Burpelson as a measure to protect this attack. Ripper's executive officer, RAF Group Captain Lionel Mandrake (on exchange from Britain), who is being held at Burpelson by Ripper, believes he knows the recall codes if he can only get a message to the outside world. Meanwhile at the Pentagon War Room, key persons including Muffley, Turgidson and nuclear scientist and adviser, a former Nazi named Dr. Strangelove, are discussing measures to stop the attack or mitigate its blow-up into an all ...

screenings.title: First We Bombed New Mexico - the Aftermath
screenings.description: The inspiring story of a relentless Latina cancer survivor who takes on 80 years of injustice by the U.S. government. Tina Cordova catalyzes a movement to secure acknowledgement and compensation for the ignored Native American and Hispanic cancer victims of the Trinity Bomb’s radioactive fallout. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH exposes the racism and nuclear colonization that enabled New Mexico to become America’s nuclear bomb–making state. The film screens during a moment of grave global insecurity. This film personalizes the unthinkable human cost of another nuclear incident. An earlier version of the film won 16 festival awards, including Best Director and Best Documentary at the Paris Cine Film Festival, Best Documentary Feature and Best Directing at the Worldwide Women’s Film Festival, and the Jury Prize for Best Historical Documentary at the San Antonio Film Festival. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH reveals an unknown story that has captured audiences. The film was a part of the momentum that led to Congress awarding compensation to New Mexico Downwinder families in 2025. The inspirational re-release witnesses a people who were once considered powerless and voiceless finally gaining recognition after years of fighting for justice.

screenings.title: Miss Representation: Rise Up
screenings.description: Over a decade after MISS REPRESENTATION exposed the media’s contribution to the underrepresentation of women in leadership, this follow-up dives deep into the cultural backlash against women’s agency and power. With the proliferation of AI and deepfakes, a new era of tech-facilitated violence is exacerbating sexism and misogyny in an attempt to control and silence women and girls. With inspiring young women at its core, MISS REPRESENTATION: RISE UP interweaves their personal journeys with powerful voices in media, culture, leadership, and academia to reimagine a future that finally uplifts women and girls.

THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

In an otherwise conservative town, this unconventional romance sparks outrage, jealousy and chaos.

screenings.title: Earth [DakhaBrakha Score]
screenings.description: Dovzhenko’s final silent feature, which depicts a clash between reactionary landowning peasants and modernizing paupers bringing the first tractor to their corner of the Ukrainian countryside, has by now spawned nearly a century of debate: is it a propagandist paean to the collectivization project in Stalin’s first Five-Year Plan, which would have catastrophic results in the Ukrainian Famine of 1932-33, or, as certain Soviet censors suspected, an on-the-sly celebration of a Ukrainian folk culture grounded in an ancient connection between the peasants and the soil they’ve so long tilled, threatened with impending erasure? What is not up for question is that Earth is among the greatest of films from the silent film canon, its distinct synthesis of Eisenstein, Pudovkin, and Vertov making it something like a summation of what had come before it, while its lyric ode to the natural world and those that live with it in harmony blazes a trail for the Ukrainian Poetic Cinema of the future to follow.

screenings.title: Afterimage
screenings.description: Powidoki Poland, 2016 Directed by Andrzej Wajda Starring Bogusław Linda Approx. 98 mins. 4K restoration. Released the year that he died at 90, Wajda’s AFTERIMAGE is the perfect coda to a career devoted to depicting the struggle between repressive governments and the free individual. Based on the life of avant-garde painter Wladysław Strzeminski, who was a target of post-War Stalinist forces, which banned abstract art in favor of state-sponsored Socialist Realism, AFTERIMAGE is a classically made drama with a commanding performance by long-time Wajda actor Bogusław Linda as the artist. Of his compulsion to make a film about Strzemiński, Wajda said, “It’s good to see what happens when art is supervised, controlled, influenced by authority and censorship.” Presented with support from The Ashes and Diamonds Fund for Eastern European Film, The Helen Frankenthaler Endowed Fund for Films on Art, and The Roy Lichtenstein Fund

In an era of automation, LAIKA delivers its most ambitious and globally accessible film yet—a bold fusion of human-crafted artistry and cinematic storytelling from the makers of Coraline.

My Undesirable Friends: Part Ii – Exile: Chapters 1-3
screenings.description: CRITIC’S PICK. “Gripping... Expect to find yourself riveted... Grand in scale but entirely intimate in scope, what she’s achieved here is a landmark work that will go down as one of the boldest documentary achievements of the 21st century.” – Ryan Lattanzio, IndieWire “A riveting and vital portrait of media courage under fire. It’s as must-see as they get.” – Nick Schager, Daily Beast CRITIC’S PICK. “Essential. Riveting.” – Alissa Wilkinson, The New York Times “Monumental... It’s great cinema.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine/Vulture “The follow-up to 2024’s LAST AIR IN MOSCOW proves every bit as compelling, if more intimate... EXILE deepens the viewer’s connection to Loktev’s journalists while introducing engaging new subjects... Funny, resilient, and vibrant, Loktev’s subjects have lost their home but not their defiant spirit.” – Tim Grierson, Screen “RIVETING. A globetrotting journey that proves harrowing in unexpected ways over an engrossing five chapters... Loktev and co-editor Michael Taylor have crafted a conversational epic that imbues each twist and turn with enormous stakes... Speaking truth to power with the online tools at their disposal, this murderer’s row consists of lively, awkward, driven, beautiful, lovestruck, and above-all complicated people, all caught in impossible personal and professional deadlocks and weighed down by immigrant uncertainty.” – Siddhant Adlakha, Variety “STAGGERING. GRIPPING. [A] massive monument to journalism, competing in length and ambition with legendary feats of nonfiction like SHOAH and the UP series... a celebration of truth in an endless fight against deception.” – Jacob Oller, AV Club “An essential chronicle of reporters under fire... Loktev, who shot the entire 12-hour doc herself, turns each reporter into the character of a real-life series unfolding before our eyes as the years go by and the war inevitably drags on... [she] creates an intimacy that goes beyond the international crises and political upheavals to focus on the human costs of an unending conflict.” – Jordan Mintzer, The Hollywood Reporter “CHILLING. The film’s final chapter has the charge of an espionage thriller.” – Marshall Shaffer, Slant “BRILLIANT. Keeping us on the edge of our seats for 6 hours. A moving tribute to the necessity of resistance.” – Boris Bastide, Le Monde

screenings.description: The inspiring story of a relentless Latina cancer survivor who takes on 80 years of injustice by the U.S. government. Tina Cordova catalyzes a movement to secure acknowledgement and compensation for the ignored Native American and Hispanic cancer victims of the Trinity Bomb’s radioactive fallout. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH exposes the racism and nuclear colonization that enabled New Mexico to become America’s nuclear bomb–making state. The film screens during a moment of grave global insecurity. This film personalizes the unthinkable human cost of another nuclear incident. An earlier version of the film won 16 festival awards, including Best Director and Best Documentary at the Paris Cine Film Festival, Best Documentary Feature and Best Directing at the Worldwide Women’s Film Festival, and the Jury Prize for Best Historical Documentary at the San Antonio Film Festival. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH reveals an unknown story that has captured audiences. The film was a part of the momentum that led to Congress awarding compensation to New Mexico Downwinder families in 2025. The inspirational re-release witnesses a people who were once considered powerless and voiceless finally gaining recognition after years of fighting for justice.

screenings.title: Dr. Strangelove Or: How I Learned to Stop Worrying and Love the Bomb
screenings.description: Paranoid Brigadier General Jack D. Ripper of Burpelson Air Force Base, believing that fluoridation of the American water supply is a Soviet plot to poison the U.S. populace, is able to deploy through a back door mechanism a nuclear attack on the Soviet Union without the knowledge of his superiors, including the Chair of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, General Buck Turgidson, and President Merkin Muffley. Only Ripper knows the code to recall the B-52 bombers and he has shut down communication in and out of Burpelson as a measure to protect this attack. Ripper's executive officer, RAF Group Captain Lionel Mandrake (on exchange from Britain), who is being held at Burpelson by Ripper, believes he knows the recall codes if he can only get a message to the outside world. Meanwhile at the Pentagon War Room, key persons including Muffley, Turgidson and nuclear scientist and adviser, a former Nazi named Dr. Strangelove, are discussing measures to stop the attack or mitigate its blow-up into an all ...

screenings.title: One in a Million
screenings.description: Filmed over ten years, ONE IN A MILLION follows Israa from childhood to adulthood on an extraordinary journey from Syria to Germany — and back again. We first meet her at age 11 as she and her family are preparing to cross the Aegean Sea, risking everything in search of safety and a better life in Europe. What unfolds is a deeply personal chronicle of war, exile and heartbreak, as Israa grows up navigating adolescence, identity and belonging far from the home she was forced to leave. As Israa settles into life in Germany, new freedoms collide with the stabilizing pull of Syrian traditions, testing bonds and reshaping her sense of self. Co-directed by Itab Azzam and Jack MacInnes, the film bears witness to the remarkable trust between filmmakers and family, following Israa and her loved ones across borders, cultures and shifting circumstances. An intimate and nuanced coming-of-age story, ONE IN A MILLION illuminates the complexities of the refugee experience while asking a universal question: what does it truly mean to call a place home?

screenings.description: Poland, 1961 Directed by Andrzej Wajda Starring Serge Merlin, Alina Janowska, Elżbieta Kępińska Approx. 115 min. Wajda’s most terrifying portrait of a desperate man at bay, as Jakub Gold, in loose parallel to the biblical character, journeys from prison after pre-war anti-Semitic riots, through hiding places during the Occupation, to fulfillment in the Resistance. Wajda’s first Scope film. Presented with support from The Ashes and Diamonds Fund for Eastern European Film, The Ada Katz Fund for Literature in Film, and The Joan S. Constantiner Fund for Jewish and Holocaust Films, donated by Leon Constantiner and Family

screenings.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
screenings.description: “One of the greatest cinematic works of creative nonfiction that I've ever seen.” – Richard Brody, The New Yorker CRITIC’S PICK. “A house party for the ages... A blissout and one of the events of this cinematic season... A deeply personal, collectively produced oral history of a specific moment of time as it was lived—and held in memory—by specific individuals. The past comes vibrantly alive in these rooms, but always circles back to the present and often points to the future... One of the sustaining pleasures of this wonderful, spirit-lifting movie is that—even with many of its contributors now gone—it feels excitingly alive.” – Manohla Dargis, The New York Times “A MASTERPIECE... A truly monumental work of art.” – Bilge Ebiri, New York Magazine “The stuff of legend... Feels like a miracle.” – Robert Daniels, RogerEbert.com “An atmospheric, electrifying documentary, and a moving testament to the importance of remembering.” – Shirley Li, The Atlantic “An intergenerational feat... A documentary brimming with the wise, the thought-provoking and the deeply entertaining... [A] glimmering gift... with something that resembles a calling forth of the ancestors... A vivid and layered time capsule... Turns viewers into time travelers but also invited guests, rightly grateful to be in the room. For some of us, this film might evoke the wonder of a great-grandchild listening in on grown-up reminiscences. Nodding at the substance. Smiling at the style.” – Lisa Kennedy, Variety “[A] rich doc crafted from gorgeously restored footage. A triumph of DIY filmmaking and an act of cinematic resistance.” – Jourdain Searles, The Hollywood Reporter “A masterpiece.” – David Fear, Rolling Stone “Not only the biggest surprise of this year’s Sundance, but a revelation.” – Chris O’Falt, IndieWire

screenings.title: Heathers
screenings.description: “Dear Diary: My teen-angst bullshit now has a body count.” A caustic rejoinder to John Hughes’s ’80s Brat Pack pictures, Lehmann’s savage suburban satire brought out the sociopathic side of Christian Slater’s too-cool outlaw persona, casting him as J.D., the motorcycle-riding new arrival at Ohio’s Westerburg High School who recruits Winona Ryder’s at-first pliable Veronica Chandler into his increasingly unhinged plans to humble their class’s ruling clique of three terrible popular girls named Heather. Clearly having a ball with Daniel Waters’s imminently quotable, coal-black screenplay, Ryder gives more than a few line-readings for the ages here; just try to keep “What’s your damage?” out of your vocabulary after viewing.

screenings.title: Fjord (Open Captioning)
screenings.description: From two-time Palme d’Or winner Cristian Mungiu, a Norwegian woman and her devout Romanian husband relocate with their five children to a remote, close-knit, coastal town. When allegations of abuse emerge, they are forced to confront a system of judgment that blurs the line between concern and prejudice.

screenings.description: ABOUT THE DOWNTOWN FESTIVAL: The Downtown Festival is a multidisciplinary celebration of independent film, music, art, and culture held across Lower Manhattan each October. Founded and directed by filmmaker Rebekah Sherman-Myntti, the festival brings together artists across disciplines and generations through film premieres, anniversary screenings, live music performances, artist talks, and special one-night-only events. Programming is led by Sherman-Myntti and Associate Director Briana Bursten, with a focus on discovery, experimentation, community, and genuine artist-to-artist exchange. The festival’s film program runs October 9-18 at Roxy Cinema, with additional programming and special events taking place all over downtown.

The eventual results pleased the General Secretary—Dovzhenko would be awarded his first of two Stalin Prizes in 1941—though the film endures less for its vigorous, saber-rattling hagiography than the moments of ineffable poetry with which it’s embroidered, rooted as always in a deep sense of Ukrainian cultural tradition and relish in the natural world. “As in all [Dovzhenko’s] best work, Shchors leaves in the memory burning images of death and of passionate life” —Jay Leyda

Consider Dvortsevoy’s similarly existential Bread Day. Sure, the rickety cart carrying the week’s delivery of bread to Township 3 of Zhikharevo barely seems to count as a train. It’s manually pushed by the pensioners who will soon argue strenuously with each other as they divvy up its contents. But their shouting is so vigorous, their insults so inventive, that questions of categorization quickly dissipate as the elderly residents, their goats in tow, battle to have the last word.” —Series curator Genevieve Yue

screenings.title: First We Bombed New Mexico - the Aftermath
screenings.description: The inspiring story of a relentless Latina cancer survivor who takes on 80 years of injustice by the U.S. government. Tina Cordova catalyzes a movement to secure acknowledgement and compensation for the ignored Native American and Hispanic cancer victims of the Trinity Bomb’s radioactive fallout. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH exposes the racism and nuclear colonization that enabled New Mexico to become America’s nuclear bomb–making state. The film screens during a moment of grave global insecurity. This film personalizes the unthinkable human cost of another nuclear incident. An earlier version of the film won 16 festival awards, including Best Director and Best Documentary at the Paris Cine Film Festival, Best Documentary Feature and Best Directing at the Worldwide Women’s Film Festival, and the Jury Prize for Best Historical Documentary at the San Antonio Film Festival. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH reveals an unknown story that has captured audiences. The film was a part of the momentum that led to Congress awarding compensation to New Mexico Downwinder families in 2025. The inspirational re-release witnesses a people who were once considered powerless and voiceless finally gaining recognition after years of fighting for justice.

When the assistant’s beautiful and outspoken wife Ganja (Marlene Clark) comes searching for her missing husband, she and Hess form an unexpected partnership. Together, they explore just how much power blood holds.

screenings.title: First We Bombed New Mexico - the Aftermath
screenings.description: The inspiring story of a relentless Latina cancer survivor who takes on 80 years of injustice by the U.S. government. Tina Cordova catalyzes a movement to secure acknowledgement and compensation for the ignored Native American and Hispanic cancer victims of the Trinity Bomb’s radioactive fallout. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH exposes the racism and nuclear colonization that enabled New Mexico to become America’s nuclear bomb–making state. The film screens during a moment of grave global insecurity. This film personalizes the unthinkable human cost of another nuclear incident. An earlier version of the film won 16 festival awards, including Best Director and Best Documentary at the Paris Cine Film Festival, Best Documentary Feature and Best Directing at the Worldwide Women’s Film Festival, and the Jury Prize for Best Historical Documentary at the San Antonio Film Festival. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH reveals an unknown story that has captured audiences. The film was a part of the momentum that led to Congress awarding compensation to New Mexico Downwinder families in 2025. The inspirational re-release witnesses a people who were once considered powerless and voiceless finally gaining recognition after years of fighting for justice.

screenings.title: Suspiria
screenings.description: Both the pinnacle of his career and the giallo subgenre, Dario Argento’s Suspiria ranks in the pantheon of the greatest horror movies of all time, and with damn good reason. Masterfully employing dream logic (the script was co-written by then wife Daria Nicolodi) and gloriously garish lighting techniques, the film is a true modern fairy tale that tells the story of a ballet student (Jessica Harper) who transfers to a German dance academy only to find it is run by a coven of murderous witches. Argento’s command of shock and suspense is on full display in every blood-soaked scene, but the true secret weapon of Suspiria is the unbelievably scary and propulsive score by the prog rock band Goblin. It all adds up to that rare witches brew: the perfect horror experience.

screenings.title: Making Marie Antoinette
screenings.description: In 2005, Eleanor Coppola filmed her daughter Sofia directing Marie Antoinette at the Palace of Versailles, the first production ever granted access to the palace. For two decades, eighty hours of footage went unseen. Now, twenty years after the film’s release and in fulfillment of her mother’s wish, that footage becomes a film of its own. Making Marie Antoinette follows the making of this landmark production, Milena Canonero’s costume work, and what it took to direct at 34, watched the whole time by her own mother.

screenings.description: One breathtaking composition follows another in Scorsese’s adaptation of Edith Wharton’s Pulitzer Prize–winning masterpiece about social mores (and taboos) amongst New York’s viperous moneyed classes in late 19th-century New York, brought to life by an all-star lineup of craftspeople including cinematographer Michael Ballhaus, editor Thelma Schoonmaker, production designer Dante Ferretti, and composer Elmer Bernstein. In front of the camera there are Daniel Day-Lewis and Michelle Pfeiffer suffering beautifully as wealthy lawyer Newland Archer and Countess Ellen Olenska, the divorced pariah whom he yearns for, and Winona Ryder as Archer’s fiancée and, eventually, wife—outwardly a winsome innocent, but a cunning, cutthroat strategist where affairs of the heart are concerned. It was, Ryder stated during a recent appearance on (of all things) Hot Ones, “The role of a lifetime.”

screenings.title: Virgina

An acutely observed study of a 19th-century peasant culture steeped in misogyny, and a strikingly sensual story of self-discovery, presented in a new 2K restoration in its NYC premiere.

screenings.title: The Only Living Pickpocket in New York
screenings.description: Harry is an old-school hustler. A classic native New Yorker, he moves through life lubricating palms with cash, relying on his wits and connections. But times are changing for Harry. His daily pickpocket take isn’t green bills and wristwatches, it’s credit cards and cell phones. And one unfortunate night, cryptocurrency and a handgun. THE ONLY LIVING PICKPOCKET IN NEW YORK is a nostalgic portrait of a small-time career criminal navigating today's digitally networked world. Writer/Director Noah Segan's modern metropolis is powered by the ephemera of a time gone by, with shoe-leather action brought to radiant life by a terrific cast, led by John Turturro's exceptional turn as Harry.

screenings.title: First We Bombed New Mexico - the Aftermath
screenings.description: The inspiring story of a relentless Latina cancer survivor who takes on 80 years of injustice by the U.S. government. Tina Cordova catalyzes a movement to secure acknowledgement and compensation for the ignored Native American and Hispanic cancer victims of the Trinity Bomb’s radioactive fallout. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH exposes the racism and nuclear colonization that enabled New Mexico to become America’s nuclear bomb–making state. The film screens during a moment of grave global insecurity. This film personalizes the unthinkable human cost of another nuclear incident. An earlier version of the film won 16 festival awards, including Best Director and Best Documentary at the Paris Cine Film Festival, Best Documentary Feature and Best Directing at the Worldwide Women’s Film Festival, and the Jury Prize for Best Historical Documentary at the San Antonio Film Festival. FIRST WE BOMBED NEW MEXICO - THE AFTERMATH reveals an unknown story that has captured audiences. The film was a part of the momentum that led to Congress awarding compensation to New Mexico Downwinder families in 2025. The inspirational re-release witnesses a people who were once considered powerless and voiceless finally gaining recognition after years of fighting for justice.

screenings.title: Ozzy & Black Sabbath: Back to the Beginning
screenings.description: OZZY & BLACK SABBATH: BACK TO THE BEGINNING documents a landmark moment in music history: Ozzy Osbourne’s historic final farewell performance for his fans at Villa Park stadium in his Birmingham hometown--captured just 17 days before his untimely passing. The film highlights the historic day with performances from Ozzy, Black Sabbath, and some of the most influential names in rock, along with personal reflections from the superstar musicians they inspired and a behind-the-scenes look at the day itself. This is an historic and intimate farewell to Ozzy and the band that changed music forever.

screenings.title: An Autumn Afternoon
screenings.description: Ozu’s gorgeous 53rd and final feature is a return to a favorite theme, the poignant comedy of marriage, with beloved regular Chishu Ryu as a father giving away his daughter and preparing for another, final goodbye. Good Morning’s satire of creeping consumerism has become more bitter here, the feeling of incoming winter chill is sharper, the entire project imbued with a tang of regret—incidentally, the title literally translates to “The Taste of Autumn Mackerel.”

screenings.title: Edward Scissorhands
screenings.description: On the heels of his Batman bonanza, Burton offered up this Tampa Bay–set modern-day fable of the title’s blade-fingered mechanical man (Johnny Depp), adopted into the suburban home of a family whose daughter (Winona Ryder) becomes the object of his gradually-requited affections. Innocent Edward inadvertently brings trouble to the neighborhood and, finally, the gift of snow on Christmas, in a film that includes the final performance by Vincent Price, and keen insight into pubescent mortification.

screenings.title: Peppermint Frappé
screenings.description: Chaplin and Saura’s electric creative partnership began with this perverse play on Alfred Hitchcock’s (already quite perverse!) Vertigo, in which meek doctor José Luis López Vázquez becomes besotted with his childhood friend’s bride (Chaplin), and sets about making over a doting assistant (Chaplin, again) at the radiology clinic where he works into the image of the woman he yearns for but cannot have. A delirious and seriously deviant psychological thriller. “I got home quite late and turned on the television; a film in Spanish with subtitles, that I knew absolutely nothing about... It was hard for me to follow and understand but, at the same time, I was convinced it was the film of a great director. I watched the rest of the film glued to the TV set and when it was over I picked up a newspaper and saw that it was Peppermint Frappé.” —Stanley Kubrick

screenings.title: Rushmore
screenings.description: Extracurricular-mad but otherwise unpromising 15-year-old student Max Fisher (Jason Schwartzman) is too busy competing (or so he thinks) with sad sack industrialist Bill Murray for the affections of teacher Olivia Williams to survive “sudden death academic probation” in Anderson’s deeply funny, deeply melancholic—and very class-conscious—sophomore feature. A back-to-school perennial, all dressed up in prep school navy blue and the muted colors of north Texas autumn, positively thrumming with the upstart energy of British Invasion anthems. (“Anderson,” noted admirer Martin Scorsese, “has a fine sense of how music works against an image.”) An irresistible, disarmingly original, delicately wrought comic fable.

screenings.title: Goodbye, Dragon Inn
screenings.description: Dir. Tsai Ming-liang. 2003, 82 mins. DCP. With Lee Kang-sheng, Chen Shiang-chyi, Kiyonobu Mitamura. It’s the last night for a crumbling Fu-Ho movie theater in Taipei, and the film is Dragon Inn (1966), the seminal wuxia by Taiwan-based filmmaker King Hu. The kinetic soundtrack contrasts the theater’s melancholy, slow-moving denizens, including a female box-office attendant with a limp, a cruising Japanese tourist, and two of the stars of Hu’s film. Filled with expertly timed sight gags, Goodbye, Dragon Inn is Tsai’s rueful backwards glance at the disappearance of the filmgoing culture of his youth—and one of the seminal films of the 21st century. The cost of admission may be applied toward a same-day purchase of a membership. Order tickets. Please pick up tickets at the Museum’s admissions desk upon arrival. All seating is general admission.

screenings.title: Manhood
screenings.description: MANHOOD follows Dallas entrepreneur Bill Moore as he attempts to make penis enlargement as commonplace as Botox. Along the way, an OnlyFans star and a father of five put their bodies — and their insecurities — on the line. Blending dark humor with unexpected empathy, MANHOOD examines shame, addiction, and the fragile myths of American masculinity.

screenings.title: Sans Soleil
screenings.description: Marker's voyage through memory, history, and video games is a free-flow of images shot largely in Japan (a cat temple, sacred phalluses, horror movies, sleeping subway riders, an animatronic JFK), with detours to Guinea-Bissau, Iceland, and, for an extended homage to Vertigo, San Francisco. An alien travelog? The world’s most profound home movie? There’s nothing quite like it in the history of cinema.

screenings.title: Cría Cuervos
screenings.description: Taking its title from the Spanish proverb “Raise ravens and they will pick your eyes out,” Saura’s lauded allegorical masterwork, set during the twilight of Spain’s Franco dictatorship, stars Ana Torrent (also seen in Spirit of the Beehive, in the same series) as a traumatized eight-year-old, second of three sisters living with a domineering aunt in Madrid following the death of their parents, who feels herself to be drifting freely between the worlds of the living and the dead and is increasingly convinced she has the ability to snuff out her adult persecutors’ lives. “Both an uncanny drama of family dysfunction and a historical parable of the end of Franco-ism… [Geraldine] Chaplin and Torrent are both outstanding.” —The Guardian

screenings.title: Ec: Nanook of the North
screenings.description: Flaherty’s pioneering ethnographic film depicts the struggle for survival of Inuit hunter Nanook and his family. Though rife with staged scenes, anachronisms, and an indulgence in the myth of the “noble savage” (Nanook was in fact an Inuit man named Allakariallak, who hunted not with harpoons and spears but with a rifle), NANOOK OF THE NORTH is a work of great lyricism, simplicity of design, and genuine affection for its protagonists, and its force is undiminished almost 100 years after it was made.

The film’s central metaphor, which suits the 21st century even better than it did the Reagan-Bush 80s, presents the wealthy as literally inhuman gluttons. Since time immemorial, this cupidinous race has parasitically feasted on the inferior homo sapiens during “shuntings,” Burroughsian nightmares of viscera, gobs of lube and denatured flesh. The mutations are the greatest showcase of the unnerving surrealistic makeup designs of Screaming Mad George—which went on to be the primary influence on the make-up designs of films like The Substance and Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil.
